set.body:
Stock JavaFX 25.0.4/26.0.2 Metal is rejected/deferred by the unchanged synthetic affine-color oracle: both 39/48 fixtures and 9/32 face-permutation failures versus the archived, correctly activated JavaFX 24 patched ES2 control at 48/48 and 0/32. Evidence: docs/verification/javafx-stock-metal-decision-20260929.md and JSON, source 7c3ff0a0, oracle plan SHA256 66cf5d0e708914708c7a287bb87b30a27514897e85581ba7e72b339072b82a37. This issue is a bounded provider investigation/qualification, not authorization to build a full JOGL backend or alter shared scientific semantics.

Consume ScalaFIM's renderer-neutral SurfaceRenderPlan, preserving original vertex/face IDs, child-to-original barycentrics, interpolated scalar/color values, threshold, opacity, missingness, legends, picking, and export semantics. Keep JOGL/OpenGL or another backend's types and lifecycle in a platform provider. First choose a minimal supported runtime and prove the same frozen 48-fixture independent color oracle at the unchanged two-channel budget, with real pipeline/API/module provenance and no private patch. Then qualify bilateral beta/FIR, at least 1,200 same-face picks per admitted scenario, 20 alternating updates, cancellation/disposal, matched lateral/medial 1x/2x/4x/8x visual matrix with named human review, and production-width painted-frame/resource measurements. Windows/Linux and consumer admission remain separate. A failed candidate must be reported as unsupported rather than silently falling back.

Acceptance: a named source/provider/runtime closure with raw receipts, passing independent scientific and native/visual/resource gates, typed fail-closed support reporting, and separate parent/consumer review. Do not infer admission from screenshot similarity or unit compilation alone.
set.title: Qualify an alternative native surface renderer against SurfaceRenderPlan
